decisions.executionNote: Establish continuous elbow-up approach with both grippers open; plan pens in white, cameras in blue, watches in red.
Approach black pen with left and rear watch with right, tilting toward top-down grasps while staying in each workspace.
Align left jaws across the pen and right around the watch; descend cautiously using wrist alignment.
Lower to grasp height and close on the black pen and rear watch. Retention remains to be verified by lifting.
Lift both grasps clear of the table to verify retention before transporting to the category baskets.
Transport the left pen toward white basket. Right watch appears unretained; reopen, recenter over its updated image location, and lower for another grasp.
Neither object is confirmed retained. Retreat left from the continuity limit and return over the black pen; right recentered watch grasp is lowered and closed.
Use smaller initial retreat steps after the zero-execution rejection; retry the centered watch grasp and reposition left over the pen.
Center left on the black pen and descend to the table-level pinch. Lift the watch slowly to check whether it follows the right gripper.
Keep both grips closed. Lift the pen for visual verification while carrying the visibly retained watch toward the red basket.
Continue category transfers with closed grips; tilt the right wrist forward to place the watch over the red interior without extending the arm to its limit.
RGB shows the pen stayed on the table and the watch slipped near the red basket. Reopen and recenter lower grasps, correcting estimated table height.
Avoid further downward contact. Recenter the left pinch using the wrist pen image; withdraw the right wrist from the basket rim toward the slipped watch.
Allow the centered pen pinch to settle and lift gently for visual verification. Lower the right jaws around the slipped watch near the basket front.
Gently lift the now-centered closed grasps and begin basket approach with a less vertical wrist to retain extension margin; verify objects follow in RGB.
Move the visibly retained pen over white basket. Right watch appears caught near the rim; lift while retreating slightly before attempting the basket transfer.
Lower and release the pen over the white interior. Raise and tilt the retained watch to clear the red rim while advancing cautiously.
The black pen is in white. Approach the white pen with left while lowering and releasing the retained watch over the red interior.
Pinch the white pen after a small wrist-image alignment correction. Withdraw right from the released watch and approach the remaining watch with open jaws.
Lift the white pen without changing its pinch orientation. Center and lower the right gripper onto the remaining watch before closing.
The white pen stayed on the table. Correct for the angled link-to-finger offset and retry its pinch. Hold then lift the watch slowly to verify retention.
Let the corrected pen pinch finish closing, then lift. Right grip closed through the watch opening; regrasp the solid watch case instead of the hollow center.
Wrist images show off-center pinches. Reopen and make small alignment corrections at grasp height: white pen toward jaw center and watch case toward the pinch line.
Finish closing without lateral motion, then make a small verification lift of both objects before any transfer.
The grasps did not retain. Make the left approach more vertical to reach the thin pen without scraping, and target the right watch's solid case at its shifted location.
Close at the corrected top-down pen alignment and let both pinches settle, then lift a short distance to check retention.
Carry the retained white pen toward white while tilting for reach margin. Reopen and lower the right pinch to the watch case at its newly shifted position.
Lower and release the retained white pen inside the white basket. Let the watch-case pinch settle, then test it with a short straight lift.
Both pens are in white. Approach the central-left camera with an open top-down grasp; raise the apparently retained watch clear of the table before transport.
Lower the left gripper over the central camera while transporting the retained watch toward red, tilting forward to maintain reach margin.
Pinch and test-lift the centered camera. Advance the retained watch over the red basket with rim clearance before releasing.
Carry the retained camera toward blue, tilting for a forward deposit. Lower and release the second watch inside red.
Place the held camera into blue. With both watches visibly in red, move the open right gripper to the remaining camera on its side of center.
Let the first camera settle in blue and withdraw left outward. Correct right alignment from the wrist view, descend, and close on the final camera.
Withdraw the empty left arm toward home with gradual wrist restoration. Let the final camera pinch settle, then test retention with a short lift.
Return left gradually to its origin. Carry the visibly retained final camera toward the right side of blue with clearance and a forward-tilted wrist.
Lower the final camera into the blue interior and open the right gripper. Finish a small left-origin correction while allowing the camera to settle.
Both cameras are visibly in blue. Withdraw the open right gripper upward and back from the rim, beginning a continuous elbow-up return to origin.
Continue the open right arm's return through its own workspace, restoring the wrist gradually while the sorted objects settle.
Finish the right-arm return with decreasing increments and both grippers open. All objects appear separated in their category baskets.
